record_notes.DCP-LETT-1864: May 2, 1856, thirteen retained blocks, annotations, full notes and bibliography read. Woodward answers an unlocated Darwin question about temporal variability with explicit hypothetical limits. Species/genus ratios 7,14,16,40 and large Conus/Pleurotoma counts are his estimates and diagnostic argument; condition of fossils adds difficulty. Half and quarter assessments of Deshayes and jokes about Gray/Pfeiffer are attributed opinions, not established species counts. Raw Mr Gray only110 has no MathML and remains a rendering hold. Island-age argument includes Madeira/St Helena/Galapagos exceptions; Terebratula comparison is negative and maximum-development generalization qualified. Book advance copy with this letter is only editorial possibility, not a proven enclosure. Darwin marginal marks are separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1875: May 15, supplied 1856, two retained blocks, full footnotes and bibliography read. This is a catalogue synopsis plus a genuine quoted Darwin extract, not a complete ALS transcription. P1 bracketed description of thanking for Supplement is cataloguer voice; only P2 is quoted Darwin praise of labour, price and service. Catalogue dates letter and publication corroborates year; no exact physical book-receipt day or letter prompt preserved. Manuscript extent3pp in metadata does not make two rendered blocks a full letter. Preserve partial target-voice eligibility P2 only.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1879: May 27, supplied 1856 with /56 endorsement, three retained blocks, full notes and bibliography read. Explicit thanks for Woodward full answer, negative Terebratula result and inability to compare genus variability over periods directly answer May 2. Hooker parallel-variable-genera information is earlier background without a specifically identified incoming source here. P2 responds to Woodward island-age doctrine, distinguishing Darwin rising volcanic islands from inferred remnants; it does not agree all islands are old continents. No book reconsideration points yet, further information intended. Intervening May 15 book acknowledgement does not replace May 2 as scientific prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1886: June 3, supplied 1856, three retained blocks, notes and bibliography read. Darwin says he has just finished close study of Woodward book; journal June 5 completion is a separate recorded event, not grounds to redate this explicit June 3 letter. Questions already written, proposed London consultation and leaving sheet if useful; no completed meeting or dispatch asserted. Later1890 is probably this sheet, but catalogued after-June4 transmission does not prove all question text was composed after Woodward invitation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1890: Darwin question memorandum, twenty retained blocks, all28 footnotes and complete bibliography read; both actual embedded drawings viewed. Catalogue afterJune4 corresponds XML June5–30, not an unlimited bound. Darwin original page-referenced questions are distinguished from Woodward answers transcribed in footnotes and Darwin subsequent pencil/crayon comments. Answers include uncertain genus identities, missing single Astarte valve, tentative Fiji location, disputed Monoceros/Struthiolaria assignments, corrected Modiolarca localities and uncertain authority for Moreton Bay. No suppression of question marks. Footnote4 has two operculum-like drawings, not a table; footnote22 has A/B/C geological schematic with arrows and quarter/half/quarter labels. No absolute durations or measurement scale. Posting and June18–21 return are editorial probabilities; exact answer/annotation dates unknown. P14 asks broadly about wide freshwater-shell ranges; this alone does not uniquely identify the different Europe/America/arctic question inferred for July15. Authored questions may predate June3 invitation, so no artificial direct training response to June4 created.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1927: July 15, 1856, twenty-six blocks including full Cyrena lists, annotations, all notes and bibliography read. Recent society paper was read July8, not yet printed; separate land/freshwater list planned for tonight. Proposes twenty named Cyrena as geographical varieties of one, based on failure to sort mixed specimens; Carpenter comparison, Lyell19-to1 and J.E.Gray dealers criticism remain reported views, not modern taxonomic facts. Retain literal reduce the reduce the duplication. Table localities and synonym qualifiers, Benson challenge and possible correction, Harvey recommendation and Pickering/Agassiz racial rhetoric remain Woodward voice. No attribution of prejudicial remarks to Darwin. Specific antecedent question about Europe/North America and Arctic occurrence is not securely identified with June1890 broad range query. Distinctive Cyrena and Harvey response clearly follows in1931.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1928: Incomplete Woodward companion memorandum, supplied July15,1856, six retained blocks including complete long shell/locality list, annotations, all notes and bibliography read. Date derives promised evening compilation in1927 and receipt by July18 response, not an independently explicit dateline. Preserve tentative synonym equals/question marks, parenthetical introductions and Arctic/altitude distinctions. Kashmir5300, Iskardo7200 and Tibetan18000-foot claim are attributed; Hooker not yet consulted. Four named shells surviving older Pliocene supply distinctive antiquity claim echoed1931. Apparatus modern synonyms do not overwrite1856 names; separate Darwin Ancient annotations are undated. No separate dispatch established and no unique surviving original question identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1931: July18,1856, five retained blocks, all footnotes read; survives as a copy, not an autograph. P1 thanks detailed writing; P2 first Cyrena clause answers1927, rest specifically answers1928 range and four-shell antiquity list. P3 already owns and has read Harvey, plans rereading first/last chapters in response to1927 recommendation. P4 states declining belief in species permanence but acknowledges weighty objections, responding within scientific exchange. Francis Darwin substituted worst for copyist rest and this for the; preserve editorial correction provenance. Farnborough address occasionally continued after Bromley change and does not redate letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13807: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Monday evening in April 1850–January 1851, crossing period boundary. Six blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Four separately enumerated specimen taxa safely arrived, one prior arcuatum valve distinguished. Woodward most likely recipient from British Museum provenance; editorial summary JWF conflicts with title/apparatus, not a certain Flower identity. Current laevis or unguis uncertainty retained despite later taxonomic distinction. Date and recipient confidence held; no exact receipt day or incoming cover text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1392: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 3, supplied 1851, inferred Woodward recipient through Aptychus discussion. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Darwin says monograph finished and printed, returns mostly named specimens with loose-valve warning. Aptychus arrived already broken, no other specimens injured; do not attribute breakage to Darwin. Return in progress not museum receipt. Printed status is author claim distinct from later distribution. Missing incoming request not required to explain unsolicited return notice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1435: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. June 9, supplied 1851. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Woodward showed paper and Darwin recalls reading/making now-lost extract, but exact paper and Annales venue uncertain; asks reference, attachment, travel and nutrition of supposed male Argonaut. Later 1852 correction identifies an arm, not whole male; no retrospective correction of current belief. Paper read at society in1845 and printed1851, probable earlier separate issue not guaranteed exact access. Summary journal volume22/pages9–22 conflicts with bibliography volume20/pages9–21, retained as source discrepancy.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1570: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. May6,1854 from later1910 catalogue. One cataloguer-authored block, four footnotes and bibliography; original letter not found.1909 exhibition guide reports Darwin refusal of Hippuritidae bridge, but no verbatim Darwin body. Carpenter1844 in guide versus1843 article in apparatus retained. This is an unavailable letter represented by synopsis, not a one-paragraph Darwin transcription or target voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1807: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Woodward memorandum after June 4, 1856, nine blocks, separate Darwin annotations, three footnotes and bibliography. Lists representative shell species with qualified identities across Europe, Greenland and North America, supplementing answers on another Darwin manuscript. Page references are to Manual of Mollusca; broader north-Atlantic land-way claim is quoted in editorial explanation of the book, not itself complete letter prose. Darwin annotation records having the note, but is undated. This does not resolve exact source of June 17 continental-island paraphrase. Preserve June 5–30 XML bounds and after-date qualification.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1889: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Woodward source June 4, 1856, nine blocks, annotations, notes and bibliography. Sharpe bereavement, credits to Waterhouse/Forbes/Hooker and request for written Darwin memoranda after May 27 discussion. Waterhouse agrees old island-fauna theory; Tasmanian sequence and migration claims differ from universal all-island continental assertion. South American islands hypothesised submerged/recolonised since older Tertiary. Whewell discussion and Pickering human-race claims attributed, not Darwin voice. Monster map and larger exposition hoped within six years, awaiting Darwin species work. Could inform 1904 P3, but main evidence does not uniquely identify this particular note over other Woodward communication; keep candidate without accepted knowledge date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1904: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. June 17–18, supplied 1856, eight blocks and full apparatus. Main text answers a missing Hooker note received June 17, weighing Huxley/Falconer/Cuvier and qualified morphological inference, with Wollaston book already read and separate missing Wollaston remark. Woodward continental-island report prompted June 16 letter to Lyell, but precise Woodward source is not fixed merely by similar subject. P7 explicitly dated 18th establishes Lyell June 17 letter known by June 18, not by June 17. P8 second postscript asks North-West American plant question and should retain its section/date context. Unidentified hand corrected ludged to lugged; no authorial correction silently inferred.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Two unlabelled outlined operculum-like structures: a larger oval with curved internal ridges and a narrow curved/claw-like form. No scale or taxon labels. Footnote4 attaches these to Woodward operculum comparison; do not mistake image for a table or infer species identity from image alone.

Geological schematic with bands labelled A,B,C, horizontal boundaries, upward arrows and an oblique cluster crossing boundaries. Fraction labels read1/4,1/2,1/4. It illustrates the period/species-duration question, with no absolute time scale or measured data; retain as diagram, not a numeric observed time series.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
